title: 36 of our published posts were removed by Instagram; the reason is not readable from here
evidence:
Instagram removed 36 of the 150 posts this app has published (24%). Measured 2026-09-24T22:25Z with `bin/rake instagram:media_inventory` (read-only; 200 media listed) and cross-checked per post with GET /{media-id}?fields=id: a gone media answers HTTP 400, code 100, subcode 33, while an id in the listing answers 200 -- that is how the set was established. An independent third source agrees: the public profile a1.sarah.a1 reports 200 posts, matching the API's media_count (200) and its /media edge (200 items).

The removed set is every post published 2026-09-05 04:00Z -> 2026-09-24 06:00Z except the daily 18:00/19:00Z slot and post 331. 25 of them vanished in ONE burst on 2026-09-24 between 18:00Z and 21:00Z: posts 315/321/329 returned real insights data at 18:00Z and are absent at 21:00Z; 16 more were marked terminal at 21:00Z after being live at 14:00Z; 5 more (300,307-310) read fine at 16:00Z. 25 is exactly the media_count drop (225 -> 200), visible between the 2026-09-24 20:00:35Z and 21:00:37Z rows of growth_snapshots. An earlier wave on 2026-09-22 20:46Z took ids 133-143 and 148.

It is NOT this repo: no delete path exists anywhere in it (only container-create, publish and insights reads touch the Graph API), and Scheduling::Commands::CollectPostInsights writes insights_unavailable_at plus one log line, nothing more. The event was invisible for two days -- the only local record was that column and a log warning; no board item and no alarm fired.

Consequence for the pre-registered gate: `zero-engagement-at-production-rate` now reads 15 of its 23 measured posts REMOVED from the account, i.e. 65% of the 14-day acceptance set is erased content. A flat zero over content the platform has deleted is not the same evidence as a zero over content that is still there, and the 2026-09-28 / 2026-10-05 GO/PIVOT/KILL verdict is read off exactly that number. The acceptance counter now carries this confound in its own evidence clause.

WHY THIS NEEDS TIM: the removal reason is not readable from here. The Graph API token cannot see it (Instagram exposes no removal-reason edge), there is no saved Instagram login for a1.sarah.a1 in the vault, and no removal notice reached tim@lawrenz.com (the persona's mailbox is elsewhere). Instagram states removal reasons and account restrictions on the login-gated Account Status page and in the account's notification inbox. One fact decides whether the growth program is being suppressed by the platform -- which nothing in this repo can obtain and which no clone/edit/re-run can substitute for.

notes.note: 2026-09-24 22:4xZ ops-triage DECISION (agent-owned, recorded here rather than deferred): KEEP PUBLISHING at the configured cadence; do not pause the account. Basis, all measured this pass from the DB: the 36 gone posts span every content pillar (6,7,8,9,16,17,18,19) and four months of history -- 5 posted 2026-05-22, 6 across 2026-05-29..06-03, 1 on 2026-08-21, 26 from 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-24 -- so this is NOT a verdict on one content class we could stop producing, and it is not an escalating new condition: it has been happening unnoticed for months, in waves (>=2 this week). No account-level restriction is visible: the account still serves 200 media, the token publishes and reads normally, and posts published after the 09-24 burst are live. Pausing would spend the one lever the program has (cadence) against no measured benefit and would leave the 09-28 gate reading a smaller, still-confounded set. The decision flips on the Account Status fact alone, which is why this item is routed to Tim and not to the growth brain. The detector and its self-closing window are in place (see platform-media-removed), and the acceptance counter now states the confound (15 of 23 measured posts gone).

2026-09-25 03:xxZ ops-triage: NEW MEASURED EVIDENCE, and it narrows the cause further without resolving it. (1) THE WAVE IS TARGETED, NOT A SWEEP: media_count fell 225->200 in ONE hour (2026-09-24 20:00Z->21:00Z) and exactly 25 of our posts are absent in the 09-05..09-24 range -- so all 25 media removed in that hour were OURS, while the account other 86 media (not ours) were untouched. A generic sweep would not pick only our content. (2) THE REMOVED SET TRACKS RENDER BATCHES, NOT PUBLISH SLOTS. Removing the publish-slot reading: each removed post asset came from a render at 08-30 10:23, 09-02 03:26-03:47 (5 posts), 09-17 04:06-05:33 (18 posts), or 09-19 15:45, plus 11 older; the renders IMMEDIATELY ADJACENT to each removed batch survived (09-02 03:05/03:18, 09-17 05:35, 09-19 16:15-17:35). The earlier publish-hour pattern was a proxy for this. (3) RULED OUT as discriminators by measurement, each a clean null: caption length and text, hashtags, content pillar, provenance/AI-mark presence and mark time, photo attributes, and publish slot. (4) CONFIRMED CAUSE FOR THE OLDER WAVE ONLY: near-duplicate images. Posts 138-142 published the SAME image on five consecutive days and all five were removed; across the hashable corpus every pair at dHash<=6 is in the removed set and no surviving pair is closer than d=7 (full numbers on the new item near-duplicate-renders-published). This does NOT explain the 25-post September wave, whose images are distinct. (5) NO REMOVAL SINCE: four consecutive per-post measurements, newly_missing=0. DECISION (agent-owned, recorded rather than deferred): the cause remains UNREADABLE from inside the repo -- the per-post API answers 400/code 100/subcode 33 with no reason field, and there is no removal timestamp anywhere -- so this item stays a tim ask for Settings -> Account Status, unchanged. It does NOT change the keep-publishing decision (the removed set spans every pillar and four months, so it is not a verdict on a content class we could stop producing). It DOES add a second, independent input to the 09-28 gate: Instagram suppresses duplicate/near-duplicate content, so near-duplication is a candidate contributor to the near-zero reach regardless of removals. No GPU claim taken, no render run, no publishing change.

ask: Log in to a1.sarah.a1 and read Settings -> Account Status (and the notification inbox): does it name a policy violation or an account restriction? A screenshot is enough -- this is the only place the removal reason exists.
